description: Figure 8(d) illustrates the performance of knowledge probing on the Qwen2.5 model after applying different editing methods. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from $10^0$ to $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", represents the accuracy in percentage, with a linear scale from 60 to 80. The plot displays five distinct lines, each corresponding to a different method: "Base" (black, solid line with circle markers), "FT" (blue, solid line with triangle markers), "MEMIT" (purple, solid line with diamond markers), "IKE" (red, solid line with square markers), and "ROME" (green, solid line with square markers). All five lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. The "ROME" method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 75% and rising to about 80%. The "MEMIT" method follows, starting at around 67% and reaching approximately 75%. The "IKE" method starts at about 65% and increases to roughly 73%. The "FT" method begins at approximately 64% and reaches about 72%. The "Base" method, representing the model without editing, starts at about 62% and increases to approximately 70%.
